new_statements.quote: Les langues gbe sont des langues à tons qui distinguent entre tons ponctuels et tons modulés. [...] Au niveau lexical, tous les dialectes gbe opposent un ton H à un ton non H. Les tons modulés n'ont pas de statut phonologique (voir Gbéto 1995a, 1997a) [...] (p. 4) — Puisque ce sont seuls les tons B et H qui sont phonologiques en maxi, je ne prendrai en compte, dans ce qui suit, que le ton B. Sur la fonction du ton M en maxi, voir Gbéto (1997a: §7). (p. 17, fn 14)
new_statements.translation: The Gbe languages are tone languages which distinguish level tones and contour tones. [...] At the lexical level, all Gbe dialects oppose a H tone to a non-H tone. Contour tones have no phonological status (see Gbéto 1995a, 1997a) [...] — Since only the tones L and H are phonological in Maxi, I will take only the L tone into account in what follows. On the function of the M tone in Maxi, see Gbéto (1997a: §7).
new_statements.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 1998/99. Description et hypothèses sur la nature de l'UPT (Unité Porteuse de Ton): l'exemple des langues gbe. Journal of West African Languages 27(2): 3-20.
new_statements.locator: p. 4 (§2.1 'Tons du gbe') and p. 17 fn 14; verified against page images ocr_jwal/ and ocr_jwal/
new_statements.rule_in_words: Maxi is a two-tone (H vs. L) tone language with a derived M tone and derived contour tones; consonant voicing conditions surface tone. The source makes no statement about word stress or accent at all — no stress rule, no denial of stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonal detail only (contour tones derived from consonantal tones; M derived from L).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/word-level tone; data are the author's own Maxi lect (Cové/Covè form, Benin). Stress is not discussed at any level.
new_statements.identity_note: All Gbéto descriptions are of the Cové/Covè (Agonlin) form of Maxi in central Benin, the author's own lect; the JWAL data are explicitly 'le parler de l'auteur' (p. 18). No separate glottocode for the Cové sub-lect in Glottolog; language-level maxi1236. Gbéto 2004 (also saved) describes Weme Gbe (weme1239), not Maxi.

sources.note: Pan-Gbe tonology whose synchronic data are largely Maxi (the author's own lect, Cové). States Gbe languages are tone languages with level and contour tones (p.4), that lexically all Gbe dialects oppose H to non-H and contour tones are not phonological (p.4), and that only B and H are phonological tones in Maxi, M being derived (p.17 fn 14, pointing to Gbéto 1997a §7). Says nothing about stress or accent (the word 'accent' occurs only in 'l'accent sera surtout mis sur' = emphasis).
